name: Administrative Building of Nestlé SA
key_features: Nestlé's headquarters in Vevey, designed by Jean Tschumi and built in 1959-1960.

name: Alcide De Gasperi building
key_features: Luxembourg's first skyscraper and tallest building, a 23-floor tower built in 1966 for the European Parliament's secretariat.

name: Kanchanjunga Apartments
key_features: Interlocking duplexes with two-storey garden verandas instead of balconies.

name: Teshima Art Museum
key_features: One concrete shell with two openings, cast over a mound of earth.

name: House NA
key_features: A glass house of 21 floor plates at different heights, like living in a tree.

name: Tate Modern
key_features: A power station turned museum; the Turbine Hall became an indoor street.

name: High Line
by: Diller Scofidio + Renfro, James Corner, Piet Oudolf
key_features: An abandoned elevated railway turned into a park in the air.

name: Pantheon
key_features: A concrete dome as wide as it is high, lit only by the oculus.

name: New Museum
key_features: Stack of shifted boxes in aluminium mesh; the offsets bring skylights down to the galleries.

name: National Taichung Theater
key_features: Curved concrete catenoid walls form a continuous cave of horizontal and vertical tubes.

name: Portugal Pavilion
key_features: A thin concrete canopy hangs like a sheet between two porticoes over a ceremonial plaza.

name: Torino Esposizioni (Hall B)
key_features: Undulating vault of prefabricated ferrocement units with glazing between the ribs.

name: Universita Luigi Bocconi Building
key_features: Office floors hang from deep concrete beams above a sunken aula, with daylight dropping through slots.

name: Gunma Museum of Modern Art
key_features: Open cubic frames clad in square aluminium panels; one wing turns off the grid over a pool.

name: Tsukuba Center Building
key_features: A sunken oval plaza inverts the Campidoglio, framed by blocks that quote fragments of past architecture.

name: Jongmyo Shrine
key_features: A long low hall of repeated bays on a broad stone platform, extended as ancestral tablets accumulated.

name: Gimnasio Maravillas
key_features: A gym under a school playground on a steep slope, with curved steel trusses that house classrooms.

name: WoZoCo
key_features: Flats that did not fit the slab hang off the north side as large timber-clad cantilevered boxes.

name: Rani ki Vav
key_features: A stepwell descending seven levels through carved stone galleries to the water table.

name: Friendship Centre
key_features: Low brick pavilions behind an earth embankment, with green roofs, courts and pools on flood-prone land.

name: Palestinian Museum
key_features: Angular stone-clad galleries follow terraced hillside gardens planted with local species.

name: Ufa-Kristallpalast
key_features: Glass crystal foyer with hanging stairs and bridges linking concrete cinema blocks.

name: German Historical Museum, Pei Wing
key_features: Glass spiral stair tower and triangular atrium link a stone wing to the baroque Zeughaus.

name: Vancouver House
key_features: Triangular footprint beside bridge ramps widens into a rectangle as the tower rises.

name: L'Oceanogràfic Restaurant
key_features: Hyperbolic paraboloid concrete shell roof over a restaurant set in water.

name: Flamengo Park
by: Roberto Burle Marx, Affonso Eduardo Reidy
key_features: Waterfront park on landfill, with curving lawns, native planting and paths along the bay.

name: Towada Art Center
key_features: Separate white boxes, one per artwork, scattered like a small town and linked by glass corridors.

name: General Archive of the Nation
key_features: Brick building around a circular courtyard with ramps, water channels and framed views.

name: Wohnstadt Carl Legien
key_features: U-shaped blocks open to the street around green courts, with coloured loggias.

name: Palazzo dello Sport
key_features: Ribbed dome of prefabricated ferrocement units above a continuous ring of glazing.

name: Scotland Street School
key_features: Twin glazed stair towers flood the stairs with light beside the sandstone classroom block.

name: Toulouse School of Economics
key_features: Brick and concrete office towers rise over garden courts, forming a compact campus like a small city.

name: Hyvinkää Church
key_features: Sharp triangular church of concrete and glass rising to a single high point.

name: Omar Khayyam Mausoleum
key_features: Interlaced rhombic frames inlaid with tiled verses rise into an open lattice crown over the tomb.

name: SESC 24 de Maio
key_features: Ramps wind up through a gutted department store to a new rooftop pool and terrace above downtown.

name: Teatro General San Martín
key_features: Glass curtain wall fronting several stacked auditoriums and a public lobby opening onto the avenue.

name: Temple of Heaven
key_features: Triple-roofed circular timber hall on a three-tier marble terrace, reached by a raised axial walkway.

name: Indian Coffee House
key_features: A cylindrical brick tower with a ramp of tables spiralling up inside perforated jali walls.

name: Le Corbusier Gymnasium
key_features: A concrete sports hall with a sloping roof and a wall that opens toward outdoor tiered seating.

name: New Baris
key_features: Mud-brick vaults and domes with wind catchers and underground air ducts for an unfinished desert market.

name: Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum
key_features: Palace rebuilt inside around top-lit galleries and a central double-height hall.

name: Nanjing International Youth Cultural Centre
key_features: Two towers and a conference podium blend into one continuous flowing ribbon at the base.

name: New Orleans Tower
key_features: A slender stone-clad residential tower rising from a low base that houses a cinema.

name: Sanctuary of Meritxell
key_features: Arcaded stone walls with tall arched openings recall regional Romanesque forms.

name: World Forum (Congress Building)
key_features: Congress hall and triangular tower with facades of coloured tiles.

name: Yokosuka Museum of Art
key_features: Glass outer skin over a steel box with round openings, partly sunk into a slope above the bay.

name: Estadio Universitario de Caracas
key_features: Baseball stands sheltered by a thin cantilevered concrete canopy free of columns.

name: Grieg Hall
key_features: Glass-fronted foyer wedge facing the city, in front of a concrete concert hall.

name: European Investment Bank
key_features: Glass vaulted envelope over V-shaped office wings and winter gardens.

name: Leopold Museum
key_features: White limestone cube with a central glazed atrium inside the MuseumsQuartier.

name: Peak Tower
key_features: Bowl-shaped roof raised on piers over the Peak Tram terminus, read against the ridge line.

name: Stadio San Nicola
key_features: Upper stands split into concrete petals with gaps between, floating over a bowl set in an earth bank.

name: Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden
key_features: A hollow concrete drum raised on four piers rings a fountain court beside a sunken sculpture garden.

name: Oscar Niemeyer Museum
key_features: A raised eye-shaped gallery on a single yellow pier above a pool, beside an earlier long concrete block.

name: Fountain Place
by: Henry N. Cobb (Pei Cobb Freed & Partners)
key_features: Faceted green-glass prism tower over a Dan Kiley water garden of cypress trees and fountains.

name: Kitakyushu Central Library
key_features: Two long copper-clad concrete barrel vaults bend across the site, bringing daylight into the reading rooms.

name: Nordic House
key_features: Low white building under a blue-glazed tiled roof whose folded profile echoes the mountains.

name: Salerno Maritime Terminal
key_features: A flowing concrete shell like an oyster, its ramps leading passengers from ticket hall to quay.

name: Oscar Niemeyer International Cultural Centre
key_features: A white dome, a curved auditorium and a slim tower stand on an open riverside plaza.

name: Tour Duo
key_features: Two leaning glass towers of different heights share a base beside the railway tracks.

name: National Museum of Ethnology
key_features: Clustered gallery blocks around a central courtyard, planned to grow in modular units.

name: Makuhari Messe
key_features: Long wave-shaped metal roof spans column-free exhibition halls beside a separate event hall.

name: Museum of Jewish Heritage
by: Kevin Roche John Dinkeloo and Associates
key_features: A hexagonal granite building with a stepped pyramidal roof on the harbour edge of Battery Park City.

name: Kurashiki City Art Museum (former City Hall)
key_features: Heavy concrete beams stacked like a log storehouse; Tange's former city hall now holds galleries.

name: Galeries Lafayette Berlin
key_features: Glass department store cored by two glass cones that reflect daylight down through every floor.

name: Kagawa Prefectural Government Office
key_features: Concrete balcony beam-ends echo timber joinery on every floor of the tower above an open pilotis lobby.

name: Marugame Genichiro-Inokuma Museum of Contemporary Art (MIMOCA)
key_features: A deep canopied forecourt facing the station is backed by a vast facade wall carrying Inokuma's mural.

name: IKMZ Library, BTU Cottbus
key_features: An amoeba-plan tower wrapped in glass printed with overlapping letters, with a brightly coloured spiral stair.

name: Torre de la Creu
key_features: Interlocking cylinders capped by trencadís-tiled domes, one rising as a tower crowned by a cross.

name: Wittgenstein House
key_features: Austere plastered cubes with tall steel doors and windows, every proportion refined by Wittgenstein.

name: Steinhaus
key_features: Shards of concrete, steel and glass break out of a lakeside slope, a built autobiography of rock and fissure.

name: The Atheneum
key_features: White panelled visitor centre where a ramp winds up through grids skewed to the town and the river.

name: Liederhalle
key_features: Concert halls with free, non-rectangular plans, the walls faced in mosaics of mixed stone and glass.

name: Utzon House, Hellebæk
key_features: Long low house: a solid brick north wall and a fully glazed south side open to the beech forest.

name: MUSE Science Museum
key_features: Sharp sloping roofs echo the mountains; a tall central void hangs animal specimens in mid-air.

name: Hagen Crematorium
key_features: Temple-like crematorium faced in black and white marble geometry, after Florentine Romanesque.

name: Istituto Marchiondi Spagliardi
key_features: A boys' reformatory with a raw concrete frame, stairs and walkways left bare and fully expressed.

name: Nemausus
key_features: Two ship-like aluminium-clad slabs on pilotis with open access galleries and generous double-height flats.

name: Retti Candle Shop
key_features: A tiny shop front of polished aluminium with a narrow keyhole-like door and mirrors that enlarge the interior.

name: Messner Mountain Museum Corones
key_features: Museum buried in a mountain summit, with only curving concrete canopies and a jutting viewing window showing.

name: Perret Tower
key_features: One of the first reinforced-concrete towers: a slender shaft of openwork concrete built for an exhibition.

name: Glaspalast Sindelfingen
key_features: Glass-walled steel hall whose transparent skin opens the sports and events floor to the town.

name: Muziekcentrum Vredenburg
key_features: Concert hall with the audience on all sides, set in a structuralist frame of repeated concrete units.

name: Skagen Odde Nature Centre
key_features: Clustered white halls with tall roof lanterns sit low among the dunes.

name: Lisbon Port Control Tower
key_features: A leaning dark prism at the mouth of the Tagus, with the glazed control room at its tilted top.

name: Gosstrakh Apartments
key_features: Early Constructivist flats: a plain block with long window bands and corner balconies, a step to Narkomfin.

name: Okanoyama Museum of Art
key_features: Tile-clad gallery boxes set in a straight line like train carriages beside the railway.

name: Garage with Chauffeur's Flat
key_features: A steel frame with bolted precast concrete panels: an early test of prefabricated building.

name: Joieria Roca
key_features: A rationalist jewellery shop whose glazed shopfront and white walls turn a Passeig de Gràcia corner.

name: Stadsschouwburg Utrecht
key_features: A brick theatre of stacked cubic volumes with a tall fly tower and long horizontal lines.

name: Pampulha Art Museum (former Casino)
key_features: A glass-walled former casino on Pampulha lake, with ramps inside and a curving dance-hall wing.

name: Geschwister-Scholl-Schule
key_features: Classrooms grouped as separate 'class homes', each with its own small garden court, off a winding hall.

name: La Congiunta
key_features: Windowless concrete gallery of linked rooms lit only from above, housing bronze sculptures.

name: Memorial to the Deportees, Yad Vashem
key_features: An original deportation cattle car stands at the end of a broken rail track cantilevered over a valley.

name: Teatro Regional del Biobío
key_features: Box of steel frames wrapped in translucent PTFE fabric that glows like a lantern at night.

name: Pousada de Santa Marinha
key_features: Monastery turned hotel, with a new granite wing of rooms added beside the old cloister.

name: Future University Hakodate
key_features: Huge glass hall of stepped studio terraces under one roof, built from precast concrete frames.

name: L'Arbre Blanc
by: Sou Fujimoto, Nicolas Laisné, Manal Rachdi
key_features: White tower bristling with long cantilevered balconies and sunshades like branches.

name: House of Music Hungary
key_features: Glass hall under a thin roof pierced by holes for trees, with a leaf-patterned golden ceiling.

name: National Monument (Indonesia)
key_features: Tall obelisk tipped with a gilded flame, rising from a square platform in Merdeka Square.

name: Hanoi Museum
key_features: Inverted stepped pyramid, each floor wider than the one below, around a spiralling ramp.

name: National Stadium, Singapore
key_features: Thin steel dome spanning the whole bowl, with a retractable roof that slides shut for shade.

name: National Theatre, Lagos
key_features: Saddle-shaped concrete hall with a folded rim, often likened to a general's cap, on an open site.

name: Odunpazarı Modern Museum
key_features: Stacked timber boxes echoing the Ottoman houses around it, around a skylit central atrium.

name: Negev Brigade Monument
key_features: Concrete sculptural landscape of a tower, dome, tunnel and water channel in the desert.

name: Torre Reforma
key_features: Two exposed-concrete walls carry the tower; a diagonal steel frame holds the glass sides.

name: Gabriel García Márquez Cultural Center
key_features: Brick terraces, ramps and a circular courtyard, open as a public route through the block.

name: Santo André Civic Centre
key_features: City hall, council chamber and theatre stand apart on a large plaza with gardens by Burle Marx.

name: King Fahd National Library
key_features: Old library wrapped in a cube of white tensile fabric diamonds held by steel cables.

name: Kaze-no-Oka Crematorium
key_features: A brick octagon, Cor-ten hall and concrete wing sit in a landscaped park, sequenced by controlled light.

name: Lycée Schorge
key_features: Laterite stone classrooms ring a courtyard, with wind towers and a screen of eucalyptus poles.

name: Magney House
key_features: Long single-room-deep pavilion under a folded corrugated-steel roof, with louvres along the north side.

name: Mapungubwe Interpretation Centre
key_features: Thin timbrel vaults of local stabilised-earth tiles rise from the landscape like rock outcrops.

name: Multihalle Mannheim
key_features: Double-curved timber lath gridshell, laid flat then pushed up into shape, covering a free-form hall.

name: Social Security Complex, Zeyrek
key_features: Small linked blocks with projecting upper floors and a concrete frame fit the old street scale.

name: Space Group Building
key_features: A dark brick office of split levels, low ceilings and small linked rooms, wrapped in ivy beside a hanok.

name: St. Louis Lambert International Airport Terminal 1
key_features: Repeated thin-shell concrete groin vaults over a column-free hall, with glazed walls between them.

name: Final Wooden House
key_features: Hut made entirely of stacked solid cedar beams that act as floor, seat and wall at once.

name: Grand Parc Bordeaux Transformation
by: Lacaton & Vassal, Frédéric Druot, Christophe Hutin
key_features: Social housing blocks extended with prefabricated winter gardens and balconies added across the facades.

name: Hu Huishan Memorial
key_features: Tent-shaped hut of bricks made from earthquake rubble, lined in pink and filled with a girl's belongings.

name: Institute of Foreign Languages
key_features: Brise-soleil walls, raised blocks and shaded walkways designed for cross-ventilation in the tropics.

name: La Collina Omihachiman
key_features: Sweets shop and café buried under a sweeping roof planted with grass.

name: La Lira Theatre Public Space
key_features: Open Corten steel canopy framing a public square on the site of a demolished theatre by the river.

name: La Tallera
key_features: Concrete lattice walls and a new plaza, with Siqueiros's murals turned to face the street.

name: Menara Tabung Haji
key_features: Round tower held by five external columns, its form drawn from a drum and the five pillars of Islam.

name: Menara UMNO
key_features: Slim tower with wing walls that catch the wind and steer it into the floors for natural cooling.

name: Mestizo Restaurant
key_features: Long black concrete roof slab resting on huge granite boulders at the edge of a park.

name: Monterrey Housing
key_features: Half-built row houses stacked as duplexes, leaving empty bays for families to fill in over time.

name: Norwegian Wild Reindeer Pavilion
key_features: Glass box with a milled pine wall shaped like eroded rock, facing across the Dovrefjell mountains.

name: Nur Alem
key_features: A glass sphere with integrated photovoltaics and wind turbines, built as the Expo 2017 national pavilion.
